claims.text: A high degree of chemical disorder in high-entropy superconducting alloys enhances local lattice distortions.
Disorder-induced local lattice distortions modulate electron–phonon coupling.
Changes in electron–phonon coupling alter critical temperature and superconducting gap magnitude relative to lower-disorder alloys.
(TaNb)1-x(ZrHfTi)x alloys can exhibit BCS-type, weak-coupling, isotropic s-wave superconductivity.
The proposed initial alloy is nearly equiatomic and single phase.
Reducing the number of constituent elements from five or more to two or three markedly reduces configurational disorder.
Random multi-element site occupancy induces local lattice strain or distortion.
Configurational disorder introduces local fluctuations in the electronic density of states.
Configurational disorder alters the phonon spectrum.
Disorder-induced changes in electronic density of states and phonons change the strength and character of electron–phonon interactions.
Electron count and degree of disorder are parameters that can affect superconductivity in refractory high-entropy-alloy analogues.
High-entropy alloys should exhibit superconducting critical temperatures and gap magnitudes distinct from matched binary or ternary baselines.
High-disorder alloys should exhibit measurable differences in electron–phonon coupling constants even when average electron count is held constant.
Disorder-modulated electron–phonon coupling is expected to dominate in single-phase, equiatomic alloys when average electronic structure is held constant.
Magnetic impurities and electron-count changes can independently affect superconductivity and therefore must be excluded from the comparison.
Competing changes in electronic density and phonon softening make the quantitative effect of disorder on Tc and gap magnitude uncertain.
The absolute disorder-induced change in superconducting parameters may be modest.
A lack of any systematic difference in superconducting parameters or electron–phonon coupling between controlled high- and low-disorder samples would falsify the proposed mechanism.
